{{nihongo|'''Ichinomiya Asama Shrine'''|浅間神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kai Province]].

'''Asama Shrine''' (Asama-jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Ichinomiya-chō Ichinomiya, {{ill|Fuefuki|Q849434|qid=Q849434}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|Q132720|qid=Q132720}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, and the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Kai Province|ckb|پارێزگای کای|cs|Provincie Kai|de|Provinz Kai|eo|Provinco Kai|es|Provincia de Kai|eu|Kai probintzia|fa|ولایت کای|fi|Kain provinssi|fr|Province de Kai|gl|Provincia de Kai|id|Provinsi Kai|it|Kai (provincia)|ja|甲斐国|ko|가이국|lt|Kajaus žemė|ms|Wilayah Kai|nl|Kai (provincie)|pt|Província de Kai|ru|Каи (провинция)|simple|Kai Province|sk|Kai (provincia)|sr|Провинција Каи|tr|Kai (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кай|wuu|甲斐国|zh|甲斐國|zh_min_nan|Kai-kok|zh_yue|甲斐國|qid=Q858076}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and it is currently a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

It is one of the many {{ill|Sengen shrine|Q3471785|qid=Q3471785}} found throughout Japan. Because it is the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Kai Province|ckb|پارێزگای کای|cs|Provincie Kai|de|Provinz Kai|eo|Provinco Kai|es|Provincia de Kai|eu|Kai probintzia|fa|ولایت کای|fi|Kain provinssi|fr|Province de Kai|gl|Provincia de Kai|id|Provinsi Kai|it|Kai (provincia)|ja|甲斐国|ko|가이국|lt|Kajaus žemė|ms|Wilayah Kai|nl|Kai (provincie)|pt|Província de Kai|ru|Каи (провинция)|simple|Kai Province|sk|Kai (provincia)|sr|Провинција Каи|tr|Kai (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кай|wuu|甲斐国|zh|甲斐國|zh_min_nan|Kai-kok|zh_yue|甲斐國|qid=Q858076}}, it is commonly known as “Ichinomiya Asama Shrine” and is also affectionately called “Ichinomiya-san.”

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine currently enshrines the following single deity:
* {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}} (konohanasakuya-hime-no-mikoto)
*: A deity who personifies Mount Fuji. She was originally one of three deities enshrined at Yamamiya Shrine, and it is said that only Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto was transferred here.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was founded in the first month of the 8th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} at the foot of the sacred mountain (present-day Sessha Yamamiya Shrine). It is said to have been transferred to its current location on the 9th day of the 12th month (lunar calendar) of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 7 ({{ill|865|Q30350|qid=Q30350}}). The surrounding area was the center of ancient {{ill|Kai Province|ckb|پارێزگای کای|cs|Provincie Kai|de|Provinz Kai|eo|Provinco Kai|es|Provincia de Kai|eu|Kai probintzia|fa|ولایت کای|fi|Kain provinssi|fr|Province de Kai|gl|Provincia de Kai|id|Provinsi Kai|it|Kai (provincia)|ja|甲斐国|ko|가이국|lt|Kajaus žemė|ms|Wilayah Kai|nl|Kai (provincie)|pt|Província de Kai|ru|Каи (провинция)|simple|Kai Province|sk|Kai (provincia)|sr|Провинција Каи|tr|Kai (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кай|wuu|甲斐国|zh|甲斐國|zh_min_nan|Kai-kok|zh_yue|甲斐國|qid=Q858076}}, and nearby remain the ruins of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kai Provincial Temple}} and {{ill|Kai Kokubun-niji|Q131909627|qid=Q131909627}}.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as one of the candidate shrines (ronsya) for “Asama Shrine of Yatsushiro District, Kai Province,” which was ranked as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}. It is also said to have been regarded as the Ichinomiya of Kai Province from the late Heian period. However, because the shrine is located in the former {{ill|Yamanashi District|Q11469930|qid=Q11469930}} and because there are other shrines that also claim to be the Ichinomiya of Kai Province, there are theories that this shrine was not actually the Myōjin Taisha or the Ichinomiya. According to the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}, following the {{ill|Jōgan eruption of Mount Fuji|Q11634546|qid=Q11634546}} of {{ill|Mount Fuji|Q39231|qid=Q39231}} in {{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}, Asama deities were enshrined in Kai Province, and in the following year, Jōgan 7 (865), on the 9th day of the 12th lunar month, Asama Shrine was built in Yatsushiro District and designated as a government shrine. It also records that another Asama Shrine was later built in Yamanashi District. For this reason, the prevailing theory is that this shrine was “the Asama Shrine later built in Yamanashi District,” though it is also possible that at the time of its founding, the area belonged to Yatsushiro District and that it was “the first Asama Shrine built in Yatsushiro District” (see “{{ill|Sengen shrine|Q3471785|qid=Q3471785}}” for details). Another view holds that the subsidiary Yamamiya Shrine was originally a shrine dedicated to the sacred mountain itself, and that as development of the Kōfu Basin progressed, the shrine moved to the village (satomiya) and was later endowed with the divine character of the Asama deity (Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto)<ref name=kamigami>“Japanese Deities,” entry on Ichinomiya Asama Shrine.</ref>.

The shrine enjoyed deep reverence from the {{ill|Takeda clan|Q1210114|qid=Q1210114}}, and many related documents have been handed down. From that period onward, historical sources referring to this shrine as the Ichinomiya and documents mentioning “Ichinomiya Estate” in the area can be found<ref>“Colophon of the Daihannyakyō held at Chōshō-ji,” copied in the latter half of April of {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 5 ({{ill|1496|Q6699|qid=Q6699}}), among others (from “Place Names of Yamanashi Prefecture”).</ref>, and it was generally revered as the Ichinomiya of Kai. Even after entering the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it continued to be protected, for example by confirmations of its landholdings from the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|Q205662|qid=Q205662}}.

=== Grounds ===
The precincts cover a little over 1 hectare. The worship hall stands behind pine trees and faces at a right angle to the approach. The worship hall was built in {{ill|1672|Q7614|qid=Q7614}} ({{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 12) during the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}. It is a single-story {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}} structure with a karahafu-style porch, measuring 7 bays by 3 bays, with a copper-sheeted roof. It is designated as a cultural property of Fuefuki City.

To the left inside the sacred fence of the main hall grows a pair of “married plum trees.” This rare variety bears two fruits from a single flower (fused at the sides) and is designated a natural monument of Yamanashi Prefecture.

Although this shrine enshrines Mount Fuji, the mountain cannot be seen from the grounds as it is hidden by the {{ill|Misaka Mountains|Q11488873|qid=Q11488873}}, and the main hall does not face in the direction of Mount Fuji.

=== Subsidiary and auxiliary shrines ===
=== Subsidiary shrine ===
[[File:YamamiyaP9130064.jpg|thumb|260px|right|{{center|Subsidiary Yamamiya Shrine main hall (National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}})}}]]
* Yamamiya Shrine (subsidiary shrine outside the grounds)
** Location: Ichinomiya-chō Ichinomiya, Fuefuki City (enclave; {{Wiki coordinates|35|38|02.31|N|138|42|50.33|E|region:JP|location|name=Yamamiya Shrine (subsidiary shrine)}})
** Enshrined deities: {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q1056122|qid=Q1056122|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|de|Ninigi|eo|Ninigi|es|Ninigi no Mikoto|fa|نینیگی-نو-میکوتو|fr|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|id|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|it|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ja|ニニギ|ko|니니기|mni|ꯅꯤꯅꯤꯒꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Ninigi|no|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|pl|Ninigi|pt|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|ru|Ниниги но Микото|simple|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|sv|Ninigi|th|นินิงิ โนะ มิโกโตะ|tl|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|tr|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|uk|Нініґі но мікото|vi|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|zh|瓊瓊杵尊|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto}} – the father and husband deities of Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto
*: Located south of the main shrine at the foot of the sacred mountain, this is the original site of Asama Shrine and corresponds to the former shrine (motomiya). Worship was conducted here from its founding in the 8th year of Emperor Suinin until the transfer on the 9th day of the 12th lunar month of Jōgan 7 (865), at which time only Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto was transferred to the village shrine (the present main shrine)<ref>“Kai Province Ichinomiya Asama Shrine Abridged History.”</ref>. Since ancient times, the Yamamiya Shinkō Festival has been held on {{ill|March 15|Q2403|qid=Q2403}}, during which a portable shrine is carried from the main shrine (now held on a Sunday around the 15th). The shrine building was rebuilt in {{ill|1558|Q6601|qid=Q6601}} ({{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 1) and is designated as a National Important Cultural Property.

=== Ōmiyuki Festival ===
The Ōmiyuki Festival is held after the Grand Annual Festival on April 15 and is commonly called “Omiyuki-san.” In ancient times it was considered the greatest festival in Kai Province. For details, see “{{ill|Shingen Embankment#Ryūō Kawarajuku and the Omiyuki Festival|Q4420072|qid=Q4420072}}.”

It began as a river-pacification (flood prevention) ritual due to the frequent great floods that struck Kai Province, during which the portable shrine is carried to Ryūō Sansha Shrine (on the {{ill|Shingen Embankment|Q4420072|qid=Q4420072}}). In the past, the procession went to Ryūō Sansha Shrine on the second Day of the Boar in April (summer procession) and to Ishida Sansha Shrine on the second Day of the Boar in November (winter procession). Along with this shrine as the Ichinomiya, the Ninomiya {{ill|Miwa Shrine (Fuefuki City)|Q11608850|qid=Q11608850|lt=Miwa Shrine}} and the Sannomiya {{ill|Tamamoro Shrine|ja|玉諸神社|qid=Q11572792|lt=Tamamoro Shrine}} participate (from the Meiji period until recent years, only this shrine participated). According to shrine tradition, the festival has been held since {{ill|Tenchō|Q1373138|qid=Q1373138}} 2 ({{ill|825|Q24624|qid=Q24624}}), but in reality it is thought to have begun sometime after the {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} era ({{ill|1558|Q6601|qid=Q6601}}–{{ill|1570|Q6659|qid=Q6659}})<ref name=kamigami/>.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties (national designation) ===
* Heart Sutra on indigo paper in gold ink (Konshi kindei Hannya Shingyō) (calligraphy)
*: A {{ill|Heart Sutra (interlinear translation)|Q622868|qid=Q622868}} that {{ill|Emperor Go-Nara|Q349467|qid=Q349467}} planned to dedicate to the Ichinomiya of various provinces in {{ill|1541|Q6516|qid=Q6516}} ({{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 10) during the Sengoku period to pray for peace. Actual dedications were made in 24 provinces, and the sutra survives today in 7 provinces including Kai. According to an ink inscription on the wrapping paper, this sutra was brought to Kai in Tenbun 19 ({{ill|1550|Q6557|qid=Q6557}}) by {{ill|Dōchō|Q7137321|qid=Q7137321}} of the Shōgoin Monzeki, and was dedicated to the Ichinomiya by the Kai provincial governor {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404|lt=Takeda Harunobu}} (Shingen). Designated on April 4, {{ill|1905|Q2047|qid=Q2047}} (Meiji 38).
* Main hall of the subsidiary Yamamiya Shrine, with four ridge tags attached (structure)
*: Located at the former shrine site (enclave). Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40).

=== Cultural properties designated by Yamanashi Prefecture ===
* Tangible cultural properties
** Tachi sword, inscription Kunitsugu (craft) – said to have been dedicated by Takeda Shingen. Designated May 13, 1965 (Shōwa 40).
** Tachi sword, inscription Ittokusai Sukenori – designated January 27, 1972 (Shōwa 47).
* Natural monuments
** Married plum trees of Ichinomiya Asama Shrine – designated November 7, 1960 (Shōwa 35).

=== Cultural properties designated by Fuefuki City ===
* Tangible cultural properties
** Worship hall, with one old material attached (structure)
** Wakatan poetry slips of Lord Takeda Shingen (calligraphy)
* Natural monuments
** Married cedar trees of Yamamiya Shrine
